rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results <U+2013> the authors grew romaine lettuce in an NFT hydroponic unit with six treatments (control, DBD plasma, nanocavitation, hybrid 3/9/15 min), five plants per treatment, 35-day cycle, and measured leaf number, fresh and dry weights, colour and flavonoid/K/Fe (Figs 4<U+2013>11, Tables 2<U+2013>3).
rows.notes: The study is a primary experiment, and it does report what the passage attributes to it: the 9-min plasma-nanobubble hybrid treatment of the nutrient solution raised shoot fresh weight by 59% and shoot dry matter by 58% (about 60% yield increase) versus control, while plasma alone and nanocavitation alone gave no significant effect, and no algae grew in the 9-min hybrid reservoir. However the claim row is labelled technology = drip, and the study involves no drip irrigation at all: it is a recirculating nutrient-film (NFT) hydroponic system with the solution treated in a plasma/nanocavitation reactor. It therefore provides no evidence on yield under drip irrigation (or MNB-water drip), so Q2 is answered no with technology_mismatch set. For the record, had the technology matched: single method (one NFT trial, one crop, one site, n=5), no intermediate variable measured (dissolved oxygen, nitrate, RONS in the solution are asserted/cited, not measured), no multi-site or farm-scale evaluation, the authors state an explicit limitation on generalizability (variations in plants, nutrient solutions, plasma generation, gas flow; small sample size and replication), and the text reports only Duncan letter groupings with no SD/CI visible in the text.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract, keywords and figure/table contents not included, so any error bars in Figs 4<U+2013>11 could not be checked). Study is a company-funded feasibility trial of plasma-nanobubble treatment of hydroponic NFT nutrient solution for lettuce; it is not an irrigation (drip) study.
